fixes.explanation: Yep. The text says this was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths had been exiled from Jerusalem (Jeremiah 29:2). So the king was on that list before the letter was sent. Even the king got carried off, friend.

Not quite, baker. Verse 2 says this was after King Jeconiah had been exiled from Jerusalem. He's in the list with the queen mother, the court officials, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths. So the king was already exiled before the letter was sent.

Whoa, whoa, whoa. That's the OPPOSITE of what the verse says, baker. The LORD says they are falsely prophesying in His name, and “I have not sent them, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:9). Nothing here says they'll turn out right. I've seen dough rise higher than that promise.

Yes, baker. The exiles were carried away from Jerusalem (Jeremiah 29:1). The LORD promises, “I will restore you to the place from which I sent you into exile.” (Jeremiah 29:14). The seventy years have an end, and the way home is part of the promise.

Nineveh is the city the prophet Jonah was sent to (Jonah 1:2), but it's not part of this promise. The exiles were carried from Jerusalem to Babylon (Jeremiah 29:1). The LORD says, “I will restore you to the place from which I sent you into exile.” (Jeremiah 29:14).
You got it, baker. The LORD says, “You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13). The finding comes when they search with all their heart.

Sacrifices? Friend, I looked all through that verse and they're not there. The LORD says, “You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13). The searching is what He names, and I'm not adding extra ingredients to His recipe.

That's right. The LORD says He will restore them from captivity and “…gather you from all the nations and places to which I have banished you, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:14). That's a promise to gather them from all the nations and places. Big promise, friend.

This one's true, baker. The LORD says, “…I will restore you from captivity and gather you from all the nations and places to which I have banished you, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:14). He promises to gather them from all the nations and places.
